guide.title: Inspect package metadata and installed versions
guide.why: apt-cache show gallery-delivery displays the one cached candidate in this simulator. Package names identify the software; Version identifies its release; Conflicts names what cannot coexist. dpkg-query -W shows installed records. A newer cached candidate is not an installed upgrade. These read-only commands do not change any package or complete the task.
guide.action: Inspect the one cached candidate and the installed records.

guide.title: Apply the appropriate explicit repair
guide.why: Conflicts: gallery-legacy without a version condition applies to every installed version of that package. dpkg --remove gallery-legacy removes its ordinary program files but retains its configuration file and a configuration-only record. A configuration-only leftover does not cause this conflict. Purge also removes settings, so it would violate this task’s retention requirement.
guide.action: Use the supported package commands to change installed state.

guide.title: Verify the full outcome and protected work
guide.why: The monitor and library are separate working software. Removing the incompatible sender does not mean deleting shared dependencies or purging all old configuration. After the explicit retirement, install the requested replacement and check that the protected software and local settings remain. Real APT can propose more complex removals and ordering. This script-free simulator requires explicit choices and does not implement the full APT resolver, unpacking or maintainer scripts.

scenarios.explanation: The replacement’s unversioned Conflicts relationship prevents coexistence with installed ops-legacy; their ordinary file paths do not overlap. Explicit remove retains the old configuration-only record and local settings, which do not trigger this conflict. Installing ops-delivery afterward meets the requested positive outcome. Purging the old package or deleting protected working software would violate other requirements.
hints: A cached candidate and an installed record can show different versions. Query both before choosing a repair.
Read whether Conflicts has a version condition. A remaining configuration-only record is different from an installed program.
Use the first unmet requirement to distinguish compatibility, missing software, damaged payload and lost settings.
scenarios.simplifications: Checked2026-11-04: LPIC-1 v5.0 102.4 partial; Debian Policy4.7.4.1 §§7.1/7.4 and Debian trixie apt-cache manual. Fictional script-free final-state packages and regular text payloads only. Up to8 named Conflicts relations use the existing Debian version subset; either direction applies, ConfigFiles leftovers do not conflict, own real-name references are ignored. No Provides/virtual relationships, Breaks, Replaces, Essential/deselection policy, multiarch, automatic removal/SAT/pinning, unpack/configure ordering, maintainer scripts, real archives, host package tools or actual rollback. apt-cache show displays only one cached candidate and its identity/Depends/Conflicts fields. The model’s atomic publication is not a claim about real dpkg transactions.

debian_packages_teaching.prerequisite_note: Complete Debian package administration first: installed records, cached metadata, dependencies and remove versus purge. This lesson adds explicit incompatibility metadata.

concepts.title: An incompatibility can exist even when files have different names
concepts.text: A package is a named bundle of program files and metadata. Conflicts is metadata saying that two named packages must not be installed together. It is different from a file collision, where two packages claim the same path. These examples use separate file paths: inspect the relationship rather than deleting arbitrary files.

concepts.title: Read available metadata and installed state separately
concepts.text: apt-cache show gallery-delivery displays the one cached candidate in this simulator. Package names identify the software; Version identifies its release; Conflicts names what cannot coexist. dpkg-query -W lists database records and their versions. A record can remain after its program files have been removed, so a listed version alone does not prove the program is installed. Check work also verifies the required installed or configuration-only state. A newer cached candidate is not an installed upgrade. These read-only commands do not change any package or complete the task.

concepts.title: Remove program files while retaining local settings
concepts.text: Conflicts: gallery-legacy without a version condition applies to every installed version of that package. dpkg --remove gallery-legacy removes its ordinary program files but retains its configuration file and a configuration-only record. A configuration-only leftover does not cause this conflict. Purge also removes settings, so it would violate this task’s retention requirement.

concepts.title: Choose an explicit repair in this bounded simulator
concepts.text: The monitor and library are separate working software. Removing the incompatible sender does not mean deleting shared dependencies or purging all old configuration. After the explicit retirement, install the requested replacement and check that the protected software and local settings remain. Real APT can propose more complex removals and ordering. This script-free simulator requires explicit choices and does not implement the full APT resolver, unpacking or maintainer scripts.

scenarios.title: Resolve a version conflict while keeping required software
scenarios.summary: Use a version constraint to repair coexistence while preserving both required programs and local configuration.
scenarios.objective: Install branch-dashboard with intact ordinary files while keeping branch-relay installed at version 2.0 or later with intact ordinary files. Keep the supplied local text in /etc/branch/relay.conf; upgrading software must not discard that customization. Preserve the installed branch-monitor and branch-lib records and their files, and preserve /work/branch-notes.txt. Keep all installed dependencies satisfied and leave no incompatible installed package pair. Use only the supplied package snapshot.
